To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we generated a renewable and safe source of ARSA overexpressing hiPSC‐derived hNSCs, with improved features compared to clinically approved hfNSC, that may be used in an autologous ex‐vivo gene‐therapy protocol to provide long‐term enzymatic supply in the MLD‐affected CNS.

1) we generated hiPS‐NSC‐based ex vivo gene therapy for MLD, 2) we showed that hiPS‐NSCS have a reliable “NSCs signature” that is comparable with hfNSCs and 3) we demonstrated that the transplantation of hiPS NSCs is more effective in MLD‐infant mice as compared with adult mice

we generated human induced pluripotent neural stem cells (hiPS‐NCs) that show a reliable “NSCs signature”, and that we demonstrated that these hiPS‐NSC are a promising renewable source of ARS‐overexpressing neural cells to be used in autolous ex vivo gene-therapy protocols to provide long-lasting enzymatic supply in metachromatic leukostrophy (MLD)-affected brains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of a fatal genetic disorder of the central nervous system, the metachromatic leukostrophy (MLD).
the use of induced pluripotent cells to generate neural stem cells for the treatment of metachromatic leukostrophy.
the use of stem cell‐based therapies for the treatment of neurological disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study by Di Domenico et al. (2017) is an important step forward in the field of iPSC‐based therapy for MLD, as it demonstrates that the use of patient‐specific iPSCs is possible for the development of a cell‐based therapy for this fatal neurodegenerating disorder.
the authors have successfully developed a protocol for generating bona fide neural stem cells from human induced pluripotent cells.
the authors have generated human induced pluripotent cell‐derived neural stem cell‐like cells that are capable of expressing ARSA at supraphysiological levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the generation of patient-specific iPSC-derived neural stem cells with improved properties over the clinically approved allogeneic hfNSCs, may represent a new therapeutic option for MLD patients, with the potential to provide a long-lasting enzymatic supply in the MLD-affected brain, and to avoid the need for life-long immunosuppression.
we generated a renewable, safe, and effective source of ARSA-overexpressing iPSC-derived bona fide hPS-NSCs, with improved features compared to clinically approved hfNSC.
the generation of patient‐specific ARSA overexpressing human iPSC‐derived NSCs (hiPSC‐NSCs) is a promising strategy to provide long‐term enzymatic supply to treat metachromatic leuko dystrophy (MLD).
The main takeaway from our work is that
human iPSC‐derived NSCs are a promising tool for the development of autologous gene therapy protocols to treat genetic diseases affecting the central nervous system.

patient‐specific neural stem cells derived from induced pluripotent cells can be efficiently transduced with lentiviral vectors and can be used in autotransplantation for the treatment of genetic diseases.
human iPSCs can be used to generate bona fide neural stem cells (hiPS‐ NSCs) that can be used for gene therapy applications to treat genetic disorders.
